domain_label: Study System — Knowledge-Graph Architect: Terminology Linking & Entity Normalization
purpose: A method for turning a raw medical/dental (and TOEFL-English) term found in card text into a normalized, catalog-linked concept with an attached definition a hover can show and a click can open — recognizing the term span in free text, normalizing synonyms/abbreviations/spelling variants to one concept identity, disambiguating competing senses under exam context, attaching a definition, and linking to the app's existing Concept catalog entry — kept honest by treating the exact source vocabulary as a research-time [METHOD] decision rather than pinning a specific standard as fact, and by grounding every app-behavior claim in APP_RECON.
assumptions: no observed dataset or gold linking set is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and every recognizer/ranker choice is an ESTIMATE synthesized from general entity-linking practice

the exact source vocabularies (which controlled medical/dental terminology to normalize against) are NOT decided here — the grounding brief marks this a research-time [METHOD: L1 research pass] decision, so this KB specifies the machinery vocabulary-agnostically and carries any named standard as [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]

this KB owns ONLY terminology linking (recognize term -> normalize synonyms -> attach definition -> link to catalog); the node/edge graph schema, hub nodes and prerequisite DAG are the other two KBs of this specialist and are out of scope here

the app's Concept and ConceptEdge entities already exist and Concept rows are find-or-created by exam_code+name [FACT-source: APP_RECON §6 / §catalog], and no hover/tooltip layer over content exists yet [FACT-source: APP_RECON §9]; this KB designs the linking data the future hover would render
exclusions: the typed knowledge-graph node/edge schema, hub-node design, prerequisite DAG and flat-spine-to-full-graph graduation (the other two kgraph KBs)
the visual rendering, layout, color-coding and force-graph interaction of the knowledge-graph view (the viz specialist) beyond naming the fields a hover consumes
training or hosting a bespoke biomedical NER/entity-linking model, and any specific vendor API contract, model name, or accuracy statistic (carried as UNKNOWN/METHOD, never fabricated)
the learner model, FSRS scheduling, weakness diagnosis and card generation (neighboring specialists) beyond consuming the concept-tag on a card as a linking hint
choosing and licensing the concrete source terminology system, which is deferred to the research pass and recorded here only as a decision with named candidate families to source-verify

glossary.definition: The task of recognizing a mention of a domain term in free text (here a flashcard's prompt/answer) and linking it to a unique entry in a reference catalog, so the same concept is identified regardless of the surface wording; the linked entry carries the definition a hover shows and the target a click opens.

A curated set of concepts each with one preferred term, a set of synonyms/variants, and usually a hierarchy of broader/narrower relations; normalizing against it collapses many surface strings to one canonical concept. Which specific medical/dental vocabulary to use is a research-time decision here, not a fixed fact.

A stable identifier standing for one concept independent of how it is written, used as the normalization target — every recognized synonym, abbreviation or spelling variant resolves to this one id. Named 'CUI-style' after the concept-unique-identifier pattern common to terminology systems [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

The bundle of surface forms — preferred label plus synonyms, abbreviations, acronyms, eponyms and spelling/inflection variants — all mapped to a single concept identity, the lookup structure that makes normalization possible.
Detecting which spans of text are domain terms, by dictionary/gazetteer matching, statistical/model tagging, or both; the step that produces candidate mentions before they are linked to concepts.

The pre-match transformation of both the dictionary and the input text — case-folding, tokenization, lemmatization/inflection stripping, punctuation and hyphenation handling, and special-character (Greek letter, accent) normalization — so surface differences do not block a match.

Choosing the intended concept when one surface form maps to several candidates, using surrounding text and domain/exam context to rank senses; e.g. a short string that means different things in a dental versus a general-English context.

The policy of attaching no link (and showing no hover) when the best candidate's confidence is below a threshold, preferring a missing definition to a confidently wrong one, since a wrong medical definition on a study card is worse than none.

Associating a short human-readable definition (a gloss) — with an optional longer definition — to a linked concept so the hover can render it; the gloss may be drawn from the source vocabulary (licensing permitting) or authored.

The metadata stored on each term-to-concept link — which source vocabulary supplied it, which match method found it (exact/fuzzy/model/manual), the confidence score, and whether a human verified it — so links can be audited, filtered and grown safely.

nodes.definition: Build the synonym set that makes normalization possible: for each concept identity, hold the PREFERRED label plus every alternate surface form — synonyms, abbreviations/acronyms, eponyms, and spelling/inflectional variants — all mapped to that one id. This is the lookup structure the recognizer matches against and the disambiguator draws candidates from [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the general entity-linking practice]. A controlled vocabulary seeds most synonyms; the app then adds exam-specific variants (dental shorthand, common misspellings) discovered during curation. Coverage of the synonym set is the single biggest lever on recognition recall — an unlisted variant is an unrecognizable term.

included: preferred label plus synonyms/abbreviations/eponyms/variants keyed to one concept id
seeding from a vocabulary then augmenting via curation
coverage as the recall lever

pros.example: listing an abbreviation, its expansion and a common misspelling so all three recognize the same concept

cons.claim: Over-broad synonym sets create ambiguity — a short or generic variant may map to several concepts and hurt precision
cons.example: adding a two-letter abbreviation that legitimately expands to three different concepts

failure_modes: missing common variants so real terms go unrecognized

nodes.definition: Specify the text normalization applied to BOTH the dictionary and the input card text before any match: case-folding, Unicode/accent normalization, tokenization, lemmatization or inflection stripping (so plurals and verb forms collapse to a base form), and punctuation/hyphenation handling (so 'x-ray', 'x ray' and 'xray' align) plus special-character mapping (Greek letters, subscripts) [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the standard NLP normalization set]. Both sides must use the SAME normalization, or a term normalized one way in the dictionary will never match the differently-normalized text. This is the cheapest, highest-leverage recall step and must be fixed before the dictionary is built, because rebuilding the dictionary under new normalization rules is costly.

included: case/Unicode/tokenization/lemmatization/punctuation/special-char normalization
applying identical normalization to dictionary and text
fixing normalization before dictionary build
excluded: the dictionary lookup algorithm itself (its own node)
approximate/fuzzy matching (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a normalization-mismatch recall gap or a new character class changes the rules

pros.claim: Symmetric normalization on both sides turns many surface differences into exact matches at near-zero cost
pros.example: a plural in card text matching the singular dictionary entry after lemmatization

cons.claim: Over-aggressive normalization can merge genuinely different terms or strip meaning, hurting precision
cons.example: stemming two distinct terms to the same root so they collide

failure_modes: normalizing text and dictionary differently so matches silently fail
over-stemming so distinct terms collapse
acceptance_tests: the normalization set is named, identical application to dictionary and text is required, and it is placed before dictionary build with the rebuild-cost rationale
revisit_triggers: recall gaps trace to a normalization mismatch

nodes.definition: Recognize terms by NORMALIZED dictionary/gazetteer lookup: index every synonym-set surface form (post-normalization) and scan the normalized card text for matches, emitting a candidate mention (span + concept id) for each hit. This is the precision-first backbone of term recognition — a match is exact against a curated list, so its false-positive rate is low [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for dictionary-based NER]. Lookup must handle multi-token entries and, when spans overlap, resolve which mention wins (deferred to the span node). Dictionary lookup is fast, interpretable and needs no training data, which suits a single-user app with a modest, curated concept set.

included: indexing normalized synonym forms and scanning text for exact hits
emitting span+concept-id candidate mentions
the precision-first, no-training-data property
excluded: longest-match resolution of overlaps (its own node)
approximate matching for misses (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a recall shortfall or recurring overlaps change the lookup design

pros.claim: Exact normalized lookup is fast, interpretable and false-positive-light with no training data, ideal for a curated single-user set
pros.example: recognizing a listed dental term instantly and knowing exactly why it matched

cons.claim: Dictionary lookup only finds what is listed, so recall is bounded by synonym-set coverage and it misses novel phrasings
cons.example: failing to recognize a valid term written in a variant no one added to the synonym set

failure_modes: low recall from incomplete synonym coverage
emitting overlapping mentions without a resolution rule
acceptance_tests: lookup indexes normalized synonym forms, scans normalized text, emits span+concept-id mentions, and is characterized as precision-first with recall bounded by coverage
revisit_triggers: recall falls below the eval target
overlaps recur and need span resolution
the synonym set grows enough to need indexing changes

nodes.definition: Resolve multi-word terms and overlapping spans: many domain terms are multi-token, and a longer term often contains a shorter listed one, so the recognizer must detect the full span and, among overlapping candidates, prefer the LONGEST match (maximal-munch) unless context says otherwise [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. Nested and adjacent terms need a documented tie-break so the same text does not emit contradictory mentions. Getting spans right matters because a mention's boundaries decide which concept — and thus which hover definition — the user sees; a truncated span links the wrong, narrower concept.

included: multi-token term detection
longest-match resolution of overlapping candidates
a documented tie-break for nested/adjacent terms
excluded: the base lookup scan (its own node)
sense disambiguation among distinct concepts (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a greedy-merge error or recurring nesting mistake changes the span rule

pros.claim: Longest-match span selection links the most specific correct concept and avoids fragmenting a term into wrong sub-terms
pros.example: recognizing a full multi-word dental term rather than only its generic head word

cons.claim: Maximal-munch is not always right, so a rigid longest-match can over-reach and merge two adjacent terms into one wrong span
cons.example: two separate listed terms sitting side by side being greedily joined into a non-term

failure_modes: truncating a multi-word term to a narrower sub-term
greedily merging adjacent distinct terms
acceptance_tests: multi-token detection and longest-match resolution are specified with a documented tie-break for nested/adjacent overlaps
revisit_triggers: a greedy merge produces a non-term
nested-term errors recur
a context rule must override longest-match

nodes.definition: Handle abbreviations and acronyms: expand short forms to their long forms and disambiguate when one short form has several expansions. A short form may be defined in-text ('long form (SF)') or be a well-known standing abbreviation; ambiguous short forms are resolved by context — the surrounding text and the card's concept-tag/exam pick the intended expansion [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for abbreviation-disambiguation practice]. Abbreviations are a high-yield but high-risk source of terms: they carry real meaning yet are the most ambiguous surface forms, so a wrong expansion produces a confidently wrong hover. Prefer in-text-defined expansions, and abstain when context cannot decide.

included: long-form expansion of short forms
in-text definition detection and standing-abbreviation lookup
context-based disambiguation of ambiguous short forms with abstain
excluded: general multi-candidate sense disambiguation (its own node)
the confidence/abstain threshold mechanics (its own node)

pros.example: expanding an in-text-defined acronym to its concept so its hover shows the right definition

cons.claim: Ambiguous abbreviations are the highest-risk surface form, and a wrong expansion yields a confidently wrong link
cons.example: a two-to-three-letter abbreviation expanded to the wrong one of several valid concepts

failure_modes: expanding an ambiguous abbreviation without enough context

acceptance_tests: long-form expansion, in-text-definition detection, context-based disambiguation and abstain-when-undecidable are all specified
revisit_triggers: a wrong-expansion error is found

nodes.definition: Recover terms that exact lookup misses via APPROXIMATE matching: character-level edit-distance for typos and minor variants, and optionally semantic/embedding similarity for paraphrases, generating candidate concepts for spans that no dictionary form matched exactly [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for approximate string matching and embedding-based candidate generation]. Fuzzy matching raises recall but injects false positives, so every fuzzy candidate is LOW-confidence by default and must clear ranking and the abstain threshold before it becomes a link. It is a fallback layer behind dictionary lookup, never the primary recognizer, and its distance/similarity cutoffs are tunable knobs traded against precision.

included: edit-distance and optional semantic similarity candidate generation
fuzzy candidates defaulting to low confidence
fuzzy as a fallback behind exact lookup
excluded: the ranking and abstain decision that gates fuzzy candidates (their own nodes)
training a bespoke matching model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a fuzzy false-positive spike or a new variant class changes the matching cutoffs

pros.claim: Approximate matching recovers typos and unseen variants that exact lookup cannot, lifting recall
pros.example: linking a misspelled dental term to the right concept via a small edit distance

cons.claim: Fuzzy matching injects false positives and can confidently link a typo to a near-but-wrong concept if not gated
cons.example: an edit-distance-one match jumping to a different real term one character away

failure_modes: treating fuzzy candidates as high-confidence links
loose cutoffs flooding the linker with false positives
acceptance_tests: edit-distance/semantic candidate generation is specified as a low-confidence fallback behind exact lookup that must clear ranking and abstain before linking
revisit_triggers: fuzzy false positives exceed the precision target
a class of variants needs a new similarity feature

nodes.definition: Compose the recognition strategy as a LAYERED cascade: exact normalized dictionary lookup first (high precision), then abbreviation resolution, then fuzzy/approximate matching as a low-confidence fallback, with an optional statistical/LLM tagger only if dictionary recall proves inadequate [ESTIMATE — to source-verify; the app already invokes a platform LLM for card generation, FACT-source: APP_RECON §generateCards, so a model tagger is feasible but is not adopted by default]. Each layer contributes candidates carrying a method tag and a base confidence, and later stages (ranking, abstain) decide what becomes a link. The cascade is chosen because it maximizes precision cheaply while keeping a recall safety net, and it degrades gracefully when the vocabulary is still the thin authored glossary.

included: the exact->abbreviation->fuzzy->optional-model cascade
per-layer method tag and base confidence
why the cascade balances precision and recall cheaply
excluded: the ranking/abstain decision that consumes candidates (their own nodes)
training or hosting a specific model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: inadequate dictionary recall or frequent layer conflicts change the cascade

pros.claim: A precision-first cascade with a fuzzy safety net gets most terms cheaply and degrades gracefully on a thin vocabulary
pros.example: exact lookup handling the bulk while fuzzy quietly recovers the occasional typo

cons.claim: Multiple layers mean multiple candidate sources to reconcile, and adding an LLM tagger raises cost and non-determinism
cons.example: two layers proposing different concepts for the same span that ranking must reconcile

failure_modes: letting a low-precision layer override exact hits
adding a model tagger before dictionary recall is proven inadequate
acceptance_tests: the layered cascade is ordered exact->abbreviation->fuzzy->optional-model, each layer tags method and base confidence, and the optional model tagger is gated on inadequate dictionary recall
revisit_triggers: dictionary recall proves inadequate
layer candidates conflict often

nodes.definition: Disambiguate when one recognized surface form maps to several candidate concepts: pick the intended sense using the surrounding text (nearby terms, the card's topic) and the concept's fit to that context [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for word-sense-disambiguation practice]. Ambiguity is common across a dental board plus an English exam — a short or generic string can be a clinical concept in one card and an ordinary English word in another. Disambiguation turns a set of candidates into a ranked best sense (or an abstention), and it is where most linking ERRORS that are not recognition errors occur, so it must record why a sense was chosen for later audit.

included: choosing among candidate concepts for one surface form
using surrounding text and card topic as disambiguation signal
recording the chosen-sense rationale for audit
excluded: the exam/concept-tag scoping signal (its own node)
the numeric ranking and abstain mechanics (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a recurring wrong-sense error or chronic context shortage changes disambiguation

pros.claim: Context-based disambiguation prevents a generic surface form from linking to the wrong sense
pros.example: resolving an ambiguous string to its dental sense on a dental card and its English sense on a TOEFL card

cons.claim: Disambiguation is the main non-recognition error source and depends on context signal that short card text may not supply
cons.example: a one-line card lacking the context needed to separate two plausible senses

failure_modes: defaulting to the most frequent sense regardless of context
linking an ambiguous term with no rationale recorded
acceptance_tests: disambiguation selects among candidates using surrounding text and card topic, yields a ranked best sense or abstention, and records the chosen-sense rationale
revisit_triggers: a recurring wrong-sense error appears

nodes.definition: Constrain the candidate space with app context: each card carries an exam_code (INBDE dental vs TOEFL English) and a concept-tag [FACT-source: APP_RECON §catalog/§CardForm], and these narrow which concepts are even plausible — a TOEFL card should rarely link a clinical dental sense, and a card already tagged to a concept biases toward that concept's neighborhood. Scoping is a cheap, high-precision prior applied before and during disambiguation [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for context-scoping practice]. It reduces ambiguity for free by shrinking the candidate set, but must be a soft prior, not a hard filter, so a genuinely cross-domain term is not wrongly excluded.

included: using exam_code and concept-tag to narrow candidates
applying scope as a soft prior before/during disambiguation
citing the app's exam and concept-tag facts
excluded: the general disambiguation ranking (its own node)
hard exclusion of cross-domain terms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a wrongly-excluded cross-domain term or a new exam changes the scoping prior

pros.claim: Exam and concept-tag scope shrink the candidate set cheaply, cutting ambiguity before ranking
pros.example: excluding clinical senses on a TOEFL card so an English word links to its ordinary sense

cons.claim: A hard scope filter would wrongly drop legitimate cross-domain terms, so scope must stay a soft, overridable prior
cons.example: a term valid in both exams being excluded because a rigid filter trusted the card's exam too much

failure_modes: treating scope as a hard filter and dropping valid cross-domain terms
ignoring the concept-tag prior that would have disambiguated
acceptance_tests: scoping uses exam_code and concept-tag as a soft prior, cites the app facts to APP_RECON, and is shown not to hard-exclude legitimate cross-domain terms
revisit_triggers: a cross-domain term is wrongly excluded
the concept-tag prior proves mis-weighted
a new exam changes the scope map

nodes.definition: Score and rank the candidate concepts for each mention into a single best link with a confidence: combine the recognition method's base confidence (exact > abbreviation > fuzzy), the disambiguation context fit, the exam/concept-tag scope prior, and synonym-form specificity into one score [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for candidate-ranking practice]. The output per mention is a ranked list whose top item, if it clears the threshold, becomes the link. Ranking centralizes every signal so the abstain decision and provenance have a single confidence to act on, and its weights are tunable against the evaluation gold set rather than guessed once and frozen.

included: combining method confidence, context fit, scope prior and specificity into one score
producing a ranked candidate list with a top confidence
tuning weights against the gold set
excluded: the abstain threshold decision (its own node)
storing the resulting provenance (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a calibration failure or a gold-set reweighting changes the ranker

pros.claim: One combined score per mention gives the abstain gate and provenance a single, tunable confidence to act on
pros.example: an exact, in-scope, context-fit candidate scoring high while a fuzzy out-of-scope one scores low

cons.claim: Combining heterogeneous signals into one score risks miscalibration, so the confidence may not mean the same thing across methods
cons.example: a fuzzy match's 0.7 not being as trustworthy as an exact match's 0.7

failure_modes: freezing hand-picked weights that never see the gold set
producing a confidence that is not calibrated across methods
acceptance_tests: ranking combines method confidence, context fit, scope prior and specificity into one score, outputs a ranked list with a top confidence, and its weights are tunable against the gold set
revisit_triggers: the confidence proves miscalibrated
the gold set shifts the best weights
a new signal is added to ranking

nodes.definition: Set the abstain policy: attach a link (and thus a hover) ONLY when the top candidate's confidence clears a threshold; otherwise abstain — no link, no hover — because on a study card a confidently WRONG medical definition is worse than a missing one [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for abstention in entity linking; the risk asymmetry is a design judgment]. The threshold is a tunable dial trading recall (more links) against precision (fewer wrong links), and it can differ by consumer: hovers demand high precision, while a low-confidence candidate can still enter the human-review queue rather than being shown. Abstention is the primary guard against the pipeline teaching the learner a wrong fact.

included: the confidence threshold for showing a link/hover
the precision-over-recall risk asymmetry on study content
per-consumer thresholds and routing low-confidence to review
excluded: the scoring that produces the confidence (its own node)
the human-review queue mechanics (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a wrong hover or too-low coverage changes the abstain threshold

pros.claim: Abstaining below threshold keeps confidently wrong definitions off study cards, the highest-value guardrail
pros.example: showing no hover for an uncertain term instead of a plausible-but-wrong definition

cons.claim: A high threshold suppresses many correct links, lowering coverage and the feature's perceived usefulness
cons.example: many valid terms left un-hovered because their confidence sat just under the cutoff

failure_modes: setting the threshold so low that wrong hovers appear
setting it so high that the feature rarely fires
acceptance_tests: the abstain policy shows a link only above threshold, states the precision-over-recall asymmetry on study content, and routes low-confidence candidates to review rather than to hovers
revisit_triggers: wrong hovers slip through
coverage is too low to be useful
a consumer needs a different threshold

nodes.definition: Attach the definition the hover will render: associate a SHORT gloss (one or two sentences) to the linked concept, with an optional longer definition for a detail view. The gloss may come from the adopted source vocabulary (if licensing permits verbatim storage — an [UNKNOWN] until the vocabulary research pass) or be authored/LLM-drafted-then-human-checked when it cannot [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the sourcing options; the app already has a platform LLM available, FACT-source: APP_RECON §generateCards]. Definitions are stored on the concept identity, not per mention, so one authored gloss serves every card that links the concept. A concept with no gloss simply yields no hover text, which the render contract must handle.

included: attaching a short gloss (plus optional long definition) to the concept identity
sourcing the gloss from vocabulary-or-authored subject to licensing
one-gloss-per-concept reuse across cards
excluded: the hover render contract that displays it (its own node)
the licensing decision itself (vocabulary-selection node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: clarified licensing or a gloss-quality challenge changes definition sourcing

pros.claim: Storing one gloss per concept identity means every card linking that concept reuses the same vetted definition
pros.example: authoring a dental term's gloss once and having it appear on all cards that mention the term

cons.claim: Licensing may forbid verbatim vocabulary definitions, forcing authored glosses whose quality must be checked
cons.example: having to rewrite a definition because the source vocabulary's text cannot be stored

failure_modes: storing definitions per mention so the same concept gets inconsistent glosses
storing verbatim vocabulary text without confirming its license
acceptance_tests: a short gloss (plus optional long form) is attached to the concept identity, sourcing is vocabulary-or-authored subject to licensing (UNKNOWN flagged), and one gloss is reused across cards
revisit_triggers: licensing for verbatim definitions is clarified
authored gloss quality is challenged
a concept needs a per-exam gloss variant

nodes.definition: Wire the click-through: a recognized mention links to the app's catalog Concept entry, so a click opens that concept's page/entry. The link binds the mention's resolved concept identity to a Concept ROW, respecting the app's find-or-create-by-exam_code+name keying [FACT-source: APP_RECON §catalog/§generateCards]; when no matching Concept exists, the pipeline either creates one under that keying or routes to review rather than inventing an unkeyed row. Because Concept is the same entity the learner model, mastery bars and (future) graph nodes hang off [FACT-source: APP_RECON §learner/§catalog], linking to it — not to a private terminology table — makes the hover, click-through, mastery and graph all point at one identity.

included: binding a mention to a Concept row for click-through
respecting find-or-create-by-exam_code+name keying
linking to the shared Concept entity so all layers share one identity
excluded: the provenance stored on the link (its own node)
the graph node/edge schema over Concept (other kgraph KBs)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: duplicate rows or a Concept-keying change alters the linkage

pros.claim: Linking mentions to the shared Concept row unifies hover, click-through, mastery and graph on one identity
pros.example: clicking a hovered term opening the same Concept the learner model tracks mastery for

cons.claim: Find-or-create keying can spawn duplicate Concepts when names differ slightly, splitting one concept across rows
cons.example: two near-identical concept names creating two rows so mastery and links fragment

failure_modes: creating unkeyed or duplicate Concept rows
linking to a private terminology table instead of the shared Concept entity
acceptance_tests: mentions bind to a Concept row under find-or-create keying (cited to APP_RECON), missing concepts create-or-route rather than inventing unkeyed rows, and the shared-identity benefit is stated
revisit_triggers: duplicate Concept rows appear

nodes.definition: Specify the DATA contract a hover consumes, independent of the UI: for a linked mention the hover needs the preferred label, the short gloss, the confidence (or a verified badge), and the click-through target (the Concept id/route). The app renders no such content hover today — the only tooltips are Recharts chart tooltips and an unused shadcn tooltip primitive [FACT-source: APP_RECON §9] — so this KB defines the fields the future hover would bind, not the component. Keeping the contract to a small field set means the terminology layer can ship its DATA before any UI exists and the viz/UX specialists can render it later without re-deriving what to show.

included: the hover data fields (label, gloss, confidence/verified, click target)
that no content hover exists yet in the app
shipping the data contract before the UI
excluded: the visual styling and interaction of the hover (viz/UX specialists)
the definition sourcing itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a UI field request or a built hover component changes the contract

pros.claim: A small stable data contract lets the terminology layer ship linking data before any hover UI is built
pros.example: emitting label+gloss+confidence+target per mention that a future component simply binds

cons.claim: Defining the contract without the real UI risks missing a field the eventual hover needs
cons.example: the UI later needing a source badge or a per-exam gloss the contract did not include

failure_modes: coupling the data contract to a specific component so it cannot be reused
omitting the confidence/verified field the UI needs to decide what to show
acceptance_tests: the contract lists label, gloss, confidence/verified and click target, notes no content hover exists yet (cited to APP_RECON), and separates data from UI rendering
revisit_triggers: the viz/UX specialist needs an extra hover field

a per-exam gloss variant is required

nodes.definition: Store PROVENANCE on every term-to-concept link: which source vocabulary supplied the concept, which match method found it (exact / abbreviation / fuzzy / model / manual), the confidence score, and a human-verified flag [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for provenance practice in curated linking]. Provenance is what lets the system filter hovers to verified-or-high-confidence links, audit why a mention linked where it did, and grow the synonym set from confirmed matches without trusting everything blindly. It also makes the pipeline honest: a link's confidence and method travel with it, so downstream consumers (hover gate, curation queue, eval) act on real metadata rather than assuming every link is equally trustworthy.

included: source-vocabulary, match-method, confidence and verified-flag metadata per link
filtering and auditing links by provenance
feeding confirmed matches back to curation
excluded: the curation queue workflow (its own node)
the ranking that computes the confidence (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a missing-provenance link or a new match method changes the metadata schema

pros.claim: Per-link provenance lets consumers filter to trustworthy links and audit any linking decision
pros.example: showing only verified-or-high-confidence links in hovers while keeping fuzzy ones for review

cons.claim: Provenance adds storage and discipline overhead, and is worthless if not consistently written on every link
cons.example: a link created without a method tag that later cannot be audited or safely trusted

failure_modes: creating links without provenance so they cannot be audited
trusting unverified fuzzy links as if human-confirmed
acceptance_tests: every link stores source vocabulary, match method, confidence and verified flag, and provenance is shown to drive filtering, audit and curation feedback
revisit_triggers: a link is found without provenance
a new match method must be recorded
auditing needs an extra provenance field

nodes.definition: Add the human-in-the-loop curation loop: route low-confidence, abstained, or newly-created-Concept links to a review QUEUE where the single owner confirms, corrects, or rejects them, and every confirmation flips the verified flag and feeds the corrected surface form back into the synonym set [ESTIMATE — design synthesis over curated-linking practice]. For a single-user study app the owner is also the curator, so the queue must be small and high-value — only genuinely uncertain links, ranked by how often the term appears — not a flood. Curation is how the linker improves over time without a training corpus: confirmed links raise coverage and precision together, and rejected ones become negative signals.

included: a review queue for low-confidence/abstained/new-Concept links
confirmation flipping the verified flag and enriching the synonym set
keeping the single-owner queue small and high-value
excluded: the batch pipeline that produces the queue (its own node)
the eval metrics that measure quality (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unmanageable queue or broken feedback loop changes the curation design

pros.claim: A small curation queue lets the single owner grow coverage and precision together without a training corpus
pros.example: confirming an uncertain link and having its surface form auto-added to the synonym set for next time

cons.claim: Curation is manual owner effort, so a queue that is too large or low-value gets abandoned and quality stalls
cons.example: flooding the owner with trivial fuzzy links until they stop reviewing entirely

failure_modes: flooding the single owner with a huge low-value queue
not feeding confirmations back so the same uncertainty recurs
acceptance_tests: low-confidence/abstained/new-Concept links route to a review queue, confirmations flip the verified flag and enrich the synonym set, and the queue is kept small and frequency-ranked for a single owner
revisit_triggers: the queue grows unmanageably large
confirmations are not feeding back to the synonym set
the owner stops reviewing

nodes.definition: Define the batch linking pipeline: scan the card corpus, run the recognition cascade, disambiguate and scope, rank and apply the abstain gate, attach definitions, bind to Concept rows, and write link annotations with provenance — as an IDEMPOTENT, re-runnable job keyed to card content, so re-running yields the same links and editing a card re-links only that card [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; parallels the app's manually-triggered pipeline pattern, FACT-source: APP_RECON §runPipeline]. Links are stored as ANNOTATIONS keyed to concept id and card, not inlined into card text, so re-linking never mutates authored content. The batch is the assembly point for every upstream node and the producer of both the hover data and the curation queue.

included: the end-to-end scan->recognize->disambiguate->rank->abstain->attach->bind->annotate batch
idempotent re-runnable, card-keyed execution
storing links as annotations, not inlined into card text
excluded: the curation queue consumption (its own node)
the eval metrics on its output (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a non-idempotency bug or authoring-latency complaint changes the batch design

pros.claim: An idempotent annotation-based batch re-links safely without mutating card text and re-processes only edited cards
pros.example: editing one card's wording and having only its links recomputed while the rest stay stable

cons.claim: A batch cadence means new or edited cards are unlinked until the next run, and the whole pipeline's quality rides on its weakest stage
cons.example: a freshly authored card showing no hovers until the linking batch next runs

failure_modes: inlining links into card text so re-runs corrupt authored content
a non-idempotent run producing different links each time
acceptance_tests: the batch runs the full recognize->rank->abstain->attach->bind chain, is idempotent and card-keyed, and stores links as annotations rather than inlining them into card text
revisit_triggers: a re-run produces different links (non-idempotency)
batch latency lags card authoring
a stage becomes the pipeline bottleneck

nodes.definition: Evaluate the linker against a GOLD set of hand-verified card mentions: measure recognition and linking PRECISION (of shown links, how many are correct), RECALL (of true terms, how many were linked), and F1, separating recognition errors from disambiguation errors so the right stage is fixed [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for entity-linking evaluation]. Because the abstain policy trades recall for precision, both must be reported at the chosen threshold, and precision on SHOWN (above-threshold) links is the metric that guards the learner from wrong hovers. The gold set is built once by the owner and grown from curation confirmations, giving a stable yardstick to tune ranking weights and thresholds instead of guessing.

included: precision/recall/F1 against a gold set
separating recognition from disambiguation errors
precision-on-shown-links as the primary safety metric
excluded: the ranking/threshold tuning the metrics inform (their own nodes)
the curation queue that grows the gold set (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a shifted gold set or a new error category changes the evaluation

pros.claim: A gold-set precision/recall/F1 evaluation gives a stable target to tune thresholds and weights against instead of guessing
pros.example: raising the abstain threshold and seeing shown-link precision improve on the gold set

cons.claim: A single-owner gold set is small and can be unrepresentative, so metrics have wide error bars early on
cons.example: a few dozen gold mentions giving a precision estimate too noisy to trust for fine tuning

failure_modes: reporting recall without the paired precision at the same threshold
tuning on a gold set too small to be representative
acceptance_tests: evaluation reports precision, recall and F1 against a gold set, separates recognition from disambiguation errors, and treats precision-on-shown-links as the primary safety metric
revisit_triggers: the gold set grows or shifts
metrics prove too noisy to tune on
a new error category needs separate measurement

nodes.definition: Compose the recommended terminology-linking approach, the go/no-go the KB builds toward. Go: a DICTIONARY-FIRST cascade (exact normalized lookup, abbreviation resolution, fuzzy fallback, optional LLM tagger only if recall demands it) over a concept-keyed synonym set; context/exam-scoped disambiguation and calibrated ranking; ABSTAIN-BY-DEFAULT hovers so a wrong medical definition never shows; definitions and click-through bound to the app's shared Concept entity with full provenance; an idempotent annotation batch feeding a small owner-curated review queue; evaluated by gold-set precision/recall/F1. No-go: do NOT pin a specific source vocabulary as fact (research-time [METHOD] decision), do NOT store verbatim vocabulary definitions before licensing is confirmed [UNKNOWN], and do NOT show low-confidence links in hovers. A link earns a hover only when it is high-confidence or human-verified, provenance-tagged, and bound to a real Concept id.

included: the go stack (dictionary-first cascade + scoped disambiguation + abstain hovers + Concept-bound links + provenance + curated batch + gold-set eval)
the no-go on pinned vocabulary, unlicensed verbatim definitions and low-confidence hovers
the earn-a-hover acceptance rule
excluded: the graph-schema verdicts of the other kgraph KBs
the hover UI styling (viz/UX)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chosen vocabulary, too-low recall, or a built hover UI changes the verdict

pros.claim: The verdict commits to the cheapest high-precision linker that fits a single-user curated app and refuses the moves that would teach a wrong fact
pros.example: shipping dictionary-first abstain-by-default linking on an authored glossary while deferring the vocabulary choice

cons.claim: A precision-first, abstain-heavy stack under-links early and defers the vocabulary and licensing calls to future research
cons.example: sparse hovers at launch because coverage waits on the researched vocabulary and curation

failure_modes: pinning a vocabulary or storing verbatim definitions against the no-go
showing low-confidence links in hovers to boost coverage
acceptance_tests: the verdict states the go stack (dictionary-first cascade + scoped disambiguation + abstain hovers + Concept-bound provenance links + curated batch + gold-set eval), the no-go on pinned vocabulary/unlicensed definitions/low-confidence hovers, and the earn-a-hover acceptance rule
revisit_triggers: the research pass selects a vocabulary and licensing

conflict_axes.name: precision_vs_recall_in_recognition
conflict_axes.description: Exact dictionary lookup is precise but misses variants, while fuzzy/model matching recovers them at the cost of false positives.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cascade exact-first with fuzzy as a gated low-confidence fallback, tuning cutoffs against the gold set

conflict_axes.name: standard_vocabulary_vs_authored_glossary
conflict_axes.description: A large controlled vocabulary gives coverage and ready definitions but adds scope and licensing burden, while an authored glossary is lean and fully controlled but thin.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run vocabulary-agnostic on an authored glossary now and swap in a researched vocabulary once coverage and licensing are confirmed

conflict_axes.name: abstain_vs_always_show_definition
conflict_axes.description: Showing a definition only above a confidence threshold protects against wrong facts but lowers coverage, while always showing one maximizes coverage at the risk of misinformation.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: abstain by default on study content and send withheld candidates to curation instead of hovers

conflict_axes.name: automatic_linking_vs_human_curation
conflict_axes.description: Fully automatic linking scales with no owner effort but ships errors, while human curation raises quality but costs the single owner's time.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: auto-link high-confidence matches and route only frequency-ranked uncertain links to a small owner queue

conflict_axes.name: longest_span_vs_granular_terms
conflict_axes.description: Preferring the longest matching span links the most specific concept but can over-merge adjacent terms, while granular spans capture sub-terms but may link too generic a concept.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to longest-match with a documented tie-break that context can override for adjacent distinct terms

conflict_axes.name: single_canonical_sense_vs_context_dependent
conflict_axes.description: Always linking a surface form to its most frequent sense is simple but wrong in off-domain contexts, while context-dependent disambiguation is right more often but needs signal short cards may lack.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use context and exam scope to pick the sense and abstain when the card lacks enough signal

conflict_axes.name: coverage_breadth_vs_licensing_risk
conflict_axes.description: Storing rich verbatim definitions from a broad vocabulary maximizes usefulness but may breach licensing, while authoring definitions avoids the risk but limits breadth and adds effort.
poles: author definitions to avoid licensing risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: confirm licensing before storing any verbatim text; author or LLM-draft-then-verify glosses until then

conflict_axes.name: inline_annotation_vs_separate_link_store
conflict_axes.description: Inlining links into card text is simple to render but couples links to content and corrupts re-linking, while a separate annotation store keeps content clean but needs join logic.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: store links as annotations keyed to concept id and card so re-linking never mutates authored text

conflict_axes.name: eager_relink_vs_stable_snapshots
conflict_axes.description: Re-linking eagerly on every card edit keeps links fresh but can churn and momentarily blank hovers, while stable snapshots are steady but go stale after edits.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-link only edited cards idempotently on the batch cadence so unedited links stay stable

edge_cases.description: A term appears only as an abbreviation with no long form anywhere in the card
edge_cases.trigger: an ambiguous short form with no in-text definition is encountered
edge_cases.mitigation: use context and exam scope to expand it; abstain and route to curation when context cannot decide

edge_cases.description: One surface string maps to two legitimate concepts (e.g. a clinical sense and an anatomical sense)
edge_cases.trigger: a genuinely ambiguous term has multiple in-scope candidates
edge_cases.mitigation: disambiguate on surrounding text; if candidates tie, abstain and queue for the owner to pick

edge_cases.description: A TOEFL English word collides with a medical term of the same spelling
edge_cases.trigger: the same string is a common English word on a TOEFL card and a clinical concept on a dental card
edge_cases.mitigation: apply exam scope as a soft prior so the English sense wins on TOEFL cards without hard-excluding cross-domain use

edge_cases.description: A multi-word term overlaps a shorter recognized sub-term
edge_cases.trigger: a longer listed term contains a shorter listed term
edge_cases.mitigation: prefer the longest match with a documented tie-break, overridable by context for adjacent distinct terms

edge_cases.description: A fuzzy match links a typo to a near-but-wrong concept one edit away
edge_cases.trigger: an edit-distance-one surface form matches a different real term
edge_cases.mitigation: keep fuzzy candidates low-confidence and require them to clear the abstain threshold or curation

edge_cases.description: A term is recognized but no matching Concept row exists yet
edge_cases.trigger: the resolved concept has no find-or-create match in the catalog
edge_cases.mitigation: create a Concept under exam_code+name keying or route to curation, never invent an unkeyed row

edge_cases.description: The source vocabulary's license forbids storing its definitions verbatim
edge_cases.trigger: licensing is confirmed restrictive during the research pass
edge_cases.mitigation: author or LLM-draft-then-verify glosses instead of storing verbatim text, and record the source in provenance

edge_cases.description: A hover fires on a linked concept that has no gloss attached
edge_cases.trigger: a concept is linked but its definition field is empty
edge_cases.mitigation: let the render contract show the label and click-through with no gloss, and queue the concept for definition authoring

edge_cases.description: A card is edited after linking, leaving stale link annotations
edge_cases.trigger: card text changes but its annotations are not recomputed
edge_cases.mitigation: key annotations to card content and idempotently re-link only edited cards on the next batch

workflow.gate: sense selection uses context and exam scope as a soft prior and records why a sense was chosen

workflow.action: Rank candidates and apply the abstain gate
workflow.description: Combine method, context and scope into one confidence and link only above the threshold, else abstain
workflow.gate: one combined confidence per mention drives an abstain-below-threshold decision that keeps wrong hovers off study content

workflow.action: Attach the definition and bind to the catalog Concept
workflow.description: Attach a short gloss to the concept identity and bind the mention to a Concept row under find-or-create keying
workflow.gate: a gloss is attached to the concept identity and the mention binds to a Concept row without inventing unkeyed rows

workflow.description: Stamp source vocabulary, match method, confidence and verified flag on each link for filtering and audit
workflow.gate: every link carries source, method, confidence and verified flag and these drive hover filtering and audit

workflow.action: Run the idempotent batch and curation queue
workflow.description: Scan the corpus, write annotation links, and route low-confidence/new-Concept links to a small owner-curated queue
workflow.gate: the batch is idempotent and annotation-based (no inlining) and produces a small frequency-ranked curation queue

workflow.action: Evaluate on the gold set and issue the verdict
workflow.description: Measure precision/recall/F1, then commit to the dictionary-first abstain-by-default Concept-bound stack with deferred vocabulary
workflow.gate: gold-set precision/recall/F1 is reported and the go/no-go verdict (dictionary-first, abstain hovers, Concept-bound provenance, no pinned vocabulary, no unlicensed definitions) is stated

priority_rationale: The problem frame, controlled-vocabulary structure, concept identity and synonym set come first because they fix what a term is normalized TO before any matching is written; text normalization, dictionary lookup, span resolution, abbreviation resolution, fuzzy matching and the layered recognition strategy come next as the recognition core that turns card text into candidate mentions; disambiguation, exam/context scoping, ranking and the abstain policy then convert candidates into trustworthy links; definition attachment, catalog linkage, the hover contract and provenance turn a link into a hover-and-click-through deliverable; and curation, the idempotent batch, evaluation and the verdict come last because they operate, grow and certify the whole pipeline, with the source-vocabulary choice deferred throughout as a research-time decision.

dominance_rules.rule: A human-verified link dominates any automatic link for the same mention
dominance_rules.rationale: owner confirmation is the highest-trust signal and should override recognizer output
dominance_rules.trigger: a mention has both an automatic candidate and a curated verified link
dominance_rules.action: use the verified link and mark its provenance human-verified

dominance_rules.rule: Abstention dominates a low-confidence guess for anything shown in a hover
dominance_rules.rationale: a confidently wrong medical definition on a study card is worse than no definition
dominance_rules.trigger: the top candidate's confidence is below the hover threshold
dominance_rules.action: show no hover and route the candidate to curation

dominance_rules.rule: Exam/context scope dominates global sense frequency in disambiguation
dominance_rules.rationale: the card's exam and concept-tag are strong priors on the intended sense
dominance_rules.trigger: a surface form's most-frequent global sense conflicts with the card's exam scope
dominance_rules.action: prefer the in-scope sense as a soft prior, abstaining if signal is insufficient

dominance_rules.rule: Exact dictionary hits dominate fuzzy matches for the same span
dominance_rules.rationale: an exact normalized match is far more reliable than an approximate one
dominance_rules.trigger: a span has both an exact and a fuzzy candidate
dominance_rules.action: take the exact candidate and treat the fuzzy one only as a low-confidence alternative

dominance_rules.rule: Longest-match spans dominate shorter nested sub-terms unless context overrides
dominance_rules.rationale: the longest listed term is usually the most specific correct concept
dominance_rules.trigger: overlapping listed terms compete for the same text
dominance_rules.action: select the longest match with a documented tie-break, letting context override for adjacent distinct terms

dominance_rules.rule: An existing Concept row dominates creating a duplicate
dominance_rules.rationale: duplicate Concepts fragment mastery, hovers and graph links across rows
dominance_rules.trigger: a resolved concept nearly matches an existing Concept by exam_code+name
dominance_rules.action: bind to the existing row under find-or-create keying rather than creating a near-duplicate

dominance_rules.rule: Confirmed licensing dominates before any verbatim definition is stored
dominance_rules.rationale: storing licensed text without permission is a legal and honesty violation
dominance_rules.trigger: a verbatim vocabulary definition is about to be stored
dominance_rules.action: store it only if licensing is confirmed permissive, else author or LLM-draft-then-verify the gloss

dominance_rules.rule: Provenance-tagged links dominate untagged links downstream
dominance_rules.rationale: consumers must know a link's method and confidence to filter and audit it
dominance_rules.trigger: a link would be written without provenance
dominance_rules.action: reject the write until source, method, confidence and verified flag are attached

dominance_rules.rule: The source-vocabulary research decision dominates dictionary construction order
dominance_rules.rationale: building the dictionary before deciding the source risks redoing it under a chosen vocabulary
dominance_rules.trigger: dictionary build is about to start before the vocabulary decision
dominance_rules.action: run on the authored-glossary fallback and keep the pipeline vocabulary-agnostic until the research pass decides

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the source vocabulary and confirm licensing before ingesting any definition text
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ingesting verbatim definitions that must be ripped out for licensing or wrong-scope reasons

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the text-normalization rules before building the dictionary
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the entire dictionary after a normalization-rule change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Store links as annotations keyed to concept id and card, never inlined into card text
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-linking corrupting authored card content and forcing a content cleanup

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the confidence/abstain threshold before wiring any hover
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping wrong hovers that must be retracted and eroding trust

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record provenance from the very first link written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a backlog of untagged links that cannot be audited or safely filtered later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish find-or-create Concept keying before creating any Concept rows from linking
anti_rework_rules.prevents: duplicate Concepts that fragment mastery and links and must be merged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the evaluation gold set before tuning the ranker or thresholds
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tuning to intuition and rediscovering regressions with no yardstick

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the hover render data contract before attaching definitions
anti_rework_rules.prevents: attaching definitions in a shape the eventual hover cannot consume

iteration_protocol.trigger: the L1 research pass selects a concrete source vocabulary and clarifies its licensing
iteration_protocol.action: swap the authored glossary for the vocabulary's synonyms and (licensing permitting) definitions and re-run the batch

iteration_protocol.trigger: gold-set precision or recall falls below the target at the chosen threshold
iteration_protocol.action: retune the ranker weights and the abstain threshold and re-evaluate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new exam or domain is added to the app
iteration_protocol.action: extend the synonym set, normalization and exam-scope map for the new domain

iteration_protocol.trigger: the curation queue reveals a recurring unrecognized variant or abbreviation
iteration_protocol.action: add the confirmed surface form to the synonym set and its expansion to abbreviation resolution
idempotently re-link only the edited cards and refresh their annotations

iteration_protocol.trigger: an ambiguous surface form recurs with wrong-sense links
iteration_protocol.action: add a disambiguation feature or scope rule and re-rank the affected mentions

iteration_protocol.trigger: a content hover UI is actually built by the viz/UX specialists
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile the hover render data contract with the real component's field needs

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
